title: The Library of Fifty Thousand Books: Man's True Wealth
summary: When a wealthy visitor asked why he spent his fortunes on second-hand books instead of gold and luxury, Ambedkar explained why an illuminated mind is the only incorruptible treasure on earth.
keywords: The Library of Fifty Thousand Books: Man's True Wealth
full_text:
In the Dadar neighborhood of Bombay stood a handsome three-story residence named **Rajgriha**.

It was the only home Dr. B. R. Ambedkar built for himself. Yet it was not an ordinary residence; it was a cathedral of knowledge housing the largest private library assembled by an individual in Asia—over **fifty thousand volumes**!

Floor-to-ceiling teak shelves groaned under the weight of world literature: jurisprudence, philosophy, political theory, anthropology, religion, and economics.

One afternoon, a wealthy merchant visited Dr. Ambedkar at Rajgriha.

Navigating narrow corridors lined with towering stacks of books, he found Ambedkar seated on a simple wooden stool, lost in deep study.

The merchant asked in bewilderment:
"Dr. Ambedkar! You are one of the most brilliant barristers in the British Empire. You could easily have amassed heaps of gold, diamond jewelry, and luxury estates.
Yet you spend every penny of your earnings importing crates of dusty books from London and New York!
What profit do these paper leaves yield you?"

Ambedkar closed his volume and smiled with serene wisdom:
"My friend! The gold and diamonds you cherish can be stolen by thieves in the night; or their market price can collapse tomorrow.
But the volume resting in my hands contains the immortal thoughts of Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Karl Marx, and the Buddha!
What thief on planet earth can break into my skull and steal these ideas from my soul?

Man does not live by bread alone; he lives by the expansion of his consciousness!
These fifty thousand books are my living children.
I have endured nights of physical starvation; but I have never spent a single night without the nourishment of a great book!
A man who possesses books can never experience loneliness, despair, or defeat!"

The merchant bowed his head in reverence.

Today, the margins of those 50,000 volumes—filled with Ambedkar's meticulous handwritten pencil annotations—stand in Mumbai as sacred monuments to the power of the human mind to overcome adversity and transform civilization.
moral: Material riches perish with the body; an illuminated intellect dedicated to human upliftment is the only immortal treasure.
